meta.title: Convert to ESM uses template strings instead of string literals
meta.fix_ref: microsoft/TypeScript#59306 (fix(59304): Convert to ESM uses template strings instead of string literals), bf39eccee6, 2024-07-16; git tag --contains: first in v5.6-beta / v5.6.2
meta.build_notes: npm typescript@5.5.4 (2024-07-22) and typescript@5.6.2 (2024-09-09), both behind typescript-language-server@4.3.3 (the latest wrapper release before 5.6.2), started with the pinned tsserver.js; the reported TypeScript version is checked on every session.
meta.notes: Not reproduced after two attempts, although attempt 2 shows the reported behaviour: pre-fix 5.5.4 converts to 'import swc from `@swc/core`;' (post-fix 5.6.2: 'import swc from "@swc/core";'). The parse probe does not flag it because TypeScript's parser accepts any expression as a module specifier; 'String literal expected' (TS1141) is a checker diagnostic, which edit_leaves_diagnostic would have seen. Probe choice error on attempt 2 (the issue calls it a syntax error); no third attempt under the two-attempt rule.

settings_note: The issue names no settings; no tsconfig.json, so tsserver uses an inferred project.

files.source: issue body, step 1 (inline code: const swc = require(`@swc/core`))
files.note: the one-line inline code of step 1 as the file; a .ts file, because the fix named in step 2 ("'require' call may be converted to an import", TS80005) is the suggestion tsserver reports for require calls in TypeScript files (in .js files it reports TS80001 'File is a CommonJS module' instead)

repro.steps: Open index.ts with 'const swc = require(`@swc/core`)' (step 1). Apply the "'require' call may be converted to an import" fix (step 2). Reported: the result uses backticks in the import statement ('import swc from `@swc/core`'), a syntax error. Probe: the fixed text must not have a parse error the original did not have.

attempts.summary: The same line in index.js: tsserver reports TS80001 ('File is a CommonJS module; it may be converted to an ES module') and no TS80005 for a .js file, so the fix named in step 2 was not offered on either build (invalid). The step-2 message identifies a TypeScript file.
